answer: An agent economy can make high-value actions depend on a stake locked in a public contract, then slash that stake when a Sybil identity is proven to have double-claimed a reward. The proof might be two signed claims tied to the same one-time task nonce, so merely inventing many identities is not enough; each must fund a separate stake and risk losing it. At the nadir of a market, this capital is costly to immobilize, while a harbor of cheap accounts or a plume of fabricated profiles brings no payout without valid claims.
